verdemorrow-seed-trials.title: Continuance trials
text: Verdemorrow Agronomics says its Continuance seed lines have now come through forty growing cycles aboard working ships, from ore haulers to salvage tugs. Crews on long runs report fresh lettuce at the galley table and fewer arguments over the last tin of beans. The company is keen to add that a grow rack is not a farm: keep the air warm, the water clean and the nutrients coming, or the rack will let you know.

Forty growing cycles aboard working ships, from ore haulers to salvage tugs, and Verdemorrow Agronomics says its Continuance seed lines have come through every one. Long-haul crews talk of fresh lettuce at the galley table and fewer fights over the last tin of beans. Verdemorrow adds a caution: a grow rack is not a farm. Keep the air warm, the water clean and the nutrients coming, or the rack will tell you about it.
mention: Verdemorrow reckon their seed has done forty cycles on working ships. Fresh lettuce every time, they say.
Heard Verdemorrow's seed has come through forty cycles on working ships. Fresh lettuce, they say. I'll believe it when I taste it.
Forty grow cycles on working ships, Verdemorrow says. Still only gets you lettuce if somebody waters it.

dwarf-wheat-shortage.title: Seed wheat short
text: Dwarf wheat is in short supply along the inner routes this quarter. Brokers blame a poor season in the Tharsis greenhouses and a rush of ship crews who have discovered fresh bread. Verdemorrow Agronomics is asking spacers who grow their own to hold back some grain for the trials rather than eat the lot.

Brokers along the inner routes report dwarf wheat in short supply this quarter, blaming a poor season in the Tharsis greenhouses and ship crews newly fond of fresh bread. Verdemorrow Agronomics asks spacers who grow their own to set some grain aside for its trials rather than eat it all.
dwarf-wheat-shortage.notes: Also the bulletin that opens the arc verdemorrow-grain-sample.
mention: Dwarf wheat is short all along the inner routes. Seems everyone has discovered bread at once.
No dwarf wheat to be had on the inner routes. Everybody's baking, apparently.
Seed wheat's scarce this quarter. Verdemorrow wants growers to save some instead of baking the lot.

galley-survey.title: Galley survey
text: A survey of long-haul crews puts a hot meal from their own galley ahead of shore leave, a working shower and, in one case, the captain. Hearth-2 owners were the most cheerful respondents, though researchers note they were also the only ones who had eaten that day.

Ask long-haul crews what beats shore leave and, says a new survey, the answer is a hot meal from their own galley, ahead of a working shower and, for one crew, the captain. Hearth-2 owners answered most cheerfully; researchers point out they were also the only ones who had eaten that day.
mention: Some survey reckons crews rate a hot meal from their own galley above shore leave. Can't say I disagree.
A survey says crews would take a hot galley meal over shore leave. Depends who's cooking, I'd say.
Galley meal over shore leave? Some survey says so. Must've been a long run.

firstlight-advert.title: Firstlight-4
text:
Verdemorrow Firstlight-4
Four trays, one crop, no excuses. Fresh greens on any ship with power, water and a crew who remembers to harvest. Verdemorrow Agronomics: where we go, life grows.

Verdemorrow Firstlight-4
Fresh greens, grown aboard. Four trays and one crop at a time, on any ship with power, water and a crew willing to harvest. Verdemorrow Agronomics: where we go, life grows.

groundwork-advert.title: Groundwork
text:
Groundwork Nutrients
Your crop cannot live on ration bars, and frankly neither should you. Groundwork charges dose by hand or through a W2 water supply. Ask for them at the supply kiosk.

Groundwork Nutrients
Plants need feeding too. Groundwork charges dose a rack by hand or through a W2 water supply, so your crop eats properly even when the crew does not. Ask at the supply kiosk.

verdemorrow-grain-sample.title: A grain sample for Verdemorrow
verdemorrow-grain-sample.notes: A short pilot arc: grow and deliver one portion of dwarf wheat grain, paid in seed and nutrients (about 75 cr of goods for a 30 cr portion). It may start once the player has a Firstlight-4 rack installed.

message.text: Hello, [player-first]. We hear the [ship] runs a Firstlight-4. Our seed trials want grain grown out here on a working ship, not in a lab. Grow some dwarf wheat and bring us one portion of grain. We pay in seed.

objective.title: Grow dwarf wheat for Verdemorrow
objective.description: Plant Continuance seed wheat in a Firstlight-4, harvest it and carry one portion of wheat grain. Seed wheat is sold at station supply kiosks.

objective.title: Take the grain to a station
objective.description: Dock at any station while carrying one portion of wheat grain. Verdemorrow collects it from there.

message.text: Sample received, and it smells like bread. Three packets of seed wheat and some Groundwork nutrients, with our thanks. Keep the [ship] growing.

line: That grow rack hums all night. I can hear it through the bulkhead.
Who put the grow rack next to my bunk? It hums like it's proud of itself.
That rack hums the whole night through. The lettuce sleeps better than I do.
What's the difference between Hearth flatbread and a ration bar? Eighty-four hours of wheat and somebody who cares.
Why's Hearth flatbread better than a ration bar? Somebody cared about it for eighty-four hours.
They say a ration bar never let anyone down. Never cheered anyone up either. Pass the flatbread.
Every time the cabin warms up I think the crop's going to cook. Then I go and check the panel again.
If the cabin gets any warmer the crop's done for. I've checked the panel three times this shift.
I dream about the grow rack overheating. That's normal, right?
Saw a hauler crew trading their own potatoes at the kiosk. Potatoes. Out here.
Some crew sold home-grown potatoes at the kiosk. Home-grown. On a ship.
There's a hauler crew out there with a potato surplus. Strangest cargo I've heard of in a while.
Old hand told me Verdemorrow started with one rack bolted into an ore hauler's galley. Probably true, the way they tell it.
They say the first Verdemorrow rack was bolted into an ore hauler's galley. Whoever did that must've been hungry.
Verdemorrow started small, I heard. One rack, one hauler, and one cook who was tired of beans.
Never name a crop before it's harvested. Everybody knows that.
Don't name the crop till it's in the bowl. Bad luck.
You named the lettuce? Before harvest? Well, it's your funeral. Its funeral, anyway.

verdemorrow-idea.text: Verdemorrow Agronomics was founded on a simple idea: a crew that grows some of its own food goes further between stations. Its line, Where we go, life grows, is printed on every seed packet it sells.

first-lettuce.text: Spacers on long hauls swear that the first fresh lettuce after a month of ration bars tastes better than anything a station galley serves.

trial-notes.text:
VERDEMORROW AGRONOMICS - CONTINUANCE TRIALS
Shipboard sample log, dwarf wheat

Sample received in good order from the [ship]. Grain dry, clean, no mould. Germination test: strong.

Field note: crews keep asking whether wheat is worth the rack space. One portion of grain is not much. A flatbread on a cold shift is another matter.

Next trials: soybeans aboard ore haulers, and whether lettuce minds the noise of a refinery next door. Volunteers welcome. Send samples to any station.

verdemorrow-agronomics.label: Verdemorrow Agronomics
verdemorrow-agronomics.title: Verdemorrow Agronomics
verdemorrow-agronomics.body:
Verdemorrow Agronomics makes equipment for growing and cooking food aboard working ships. Its name is meant to suggest green growth and tomorrow, and its line, Where we go, life grows, is printed on every seed packet.

The company sells four lines. Firstlight cultivation racks grow a crop in four trays under their own lights. Hearth galley cookers turn produce into meals. Continuance is planting stock: seed potatoes and seed packets. Groundwork covers nutrients, water supply units and the benches that recover nutrients from crop waste.

Verdemorrow's pitch is modest by station standards. A rack will not feed a crew on its own, but fresh food, a little less to buy at each dock and something growing aboard make a long run easier.

growing-food-aboard.label: Growing food aboard
growing-food-aboard.title: Growing food aboard
growing-food-aboard.body:
A grow rack needs what a crew needs, only more steadily: power, water, warm air at a comfortable pressure, and a little carbon dioxide, which people breathe out anyway. Add nutrients, plant the seed and keep the cabin steady until harvest.

Most of what goes wrong is the room, not the plant. A cabin that gets too hot or too cold stops a crop growing, and one left that way long enough loses it. The rack's panel says what it is waiting for.

Nothing grown aboard is free. Every kilogram of food comes from water, nutrients, carbon from the air and the electricity that lights the trays, and what the crop does not use ends up as residue to deal with.
